The new helper returns `refreshTokenResponse`, a `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed tokens — so the SafeParse wrapper is persisted, corrupting stored Google credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` is later persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error? }`), not the parsed credential payload itself. Therefore this update would store the wrapper object instead of the actual credentials (`refreshTokenResponse.data`), corrupting the credential `key` structure.
